narrative:
The October close starts with 10.0M records across 12 close feeds and NOK 1,357M of value under close. In September — the first close on Business Central — the API timed out under month-end volume and the team rebuilt the books from the Data Lake by hand. That is why the close ran to WD+11.

This month, agents pull Business Central, the new POS, the web shop and the Data Lake in parallel and at full volume, and check every feed against the BC trial balance before matching starts. Completeness is 96.8% at WD+1. The gaps sit in the BC General Ledger (91.2%) and store-owner intercompany (93.8%), where throttling hit hardest, and in late stock-count files from East franchise stores.

Three backfill proposals are waiting. Accepting them lifts Group & Shared Services above the 98% SLA, so the controllers start reconciling from complete data rather than chasing missing files.

signals.title: September close — Business Central API time-outs
signals.excerpt: The Business Central API could not handle the data volume during the first month-end close on the new ERP. Finance fell back to extracting from the Data Lake to finish the close.

signals.title: New POS roll-out — cut-over plan
signals.excerpt: POS replacement rolling out chain by chain alongside the Business Central implementation with Tietoevry. Item master moves to EAN; settlement files change format at cut-over.

signals.title: Reliance on external consultants
signals.excerpt: Close workarounds depend on consultant scripts with limited documentation. Knowledge leaves when consultants roll off.
